experiments.scope: B' runs 0, 1 of pre-registration A (proof 4.4). For each advice k in turn (trials 2q, 2q+1 for the q-th): trial 2q re-runs, from the run's label alone, the setup of the candidate c that produced the advice and its accepting attempt j (BRUNS[k]); PASS iff the setup's row-operation count, the attempt's status, DF and row count, and SHA-256 of the output advice equal the log (the budget counter itself is executed by r5-bpfull). Trial 2q+1 re-runs one other logged attempt j' < j of the same candidate, chosen by SHA-256 of the trial seed; PASS iff status, DF and row count match. Then trials 4..67 run one connector attempt each (cap X_MAX = 2^23 work units, DMIN 33) on advice k = ks[t mod 2] with coin words from the organizer seed (class Coins); PASS iff accepted and two sampled solutions satisfy Lemmas 1-2 (proof 2.5), FAIL otherwise; the facts of proof 3 for that advice are checked first. Other trials return no pair. PASS = (00^135, 01||00^134) satisfies the declared event; FAIL = (00^135, 02||00^134) does not. Both are fixed sentinels, so the host check is vacuous; the evidence is the organizer's execution of the visible code, and the host-counted numbers are successes (PASS) and returned_pairs (PASS + FAIL).

experiments.scope: Exact recount of the trail search P (proof 2.1) for start lanes 0, 1. Trial 0 runs T1 (the depth-first search of in-kernel cores of at most 10 bits) from bit (lane, z = 0) of each lane of the group, counting every node, and for each core found whose smallest lane is in the group computes C1 (alpha4 compatible with beta3 = T2 leaves), decides P45 > 0 exactly (pruned search over the same alpha4), and, if P45 > 0, computes C2 (beta2 compatible with alpha3 = T3 leaves) and T3's batch layout (proof 2.1: batches and groups). PASS iff the per-lane node counts and the group totals equal GROUP_LOG. The groups 0..3 (lanes 0-1, 2-7, 8-16, 17-24) partition the cores; P45 > 0 is decided by a depth-first search that remembers failed partial states. Other trials return no pair. PASS = (00^135, 01||00^134) satisfies the declared event; FAIL = (00^135, 02||00^134) does not. Both are fixed sentinels, so the host check is vacuous; the evidence is the organizer's execution of the visible code, and the host-counted numbers are successes (PASS) and returned_pairs (PASS + FAIL).
experiments.hypothesis: P's counts that enter the time bound are exact. Predicted: PASS with 692,664 nodes, 1023 cores, sum C1 = 974,737,408, 204 cores with P45 > 0, sum C2 = 608,900,651,514, 2,507,358,321 T3 batches in 616 groups. Over r5-trail-0..3: 8,674,833 nodes, 1741 cores, C1 = 1,639,088,128, 467 kept cores, C2 = 1,379,275,399,350, 5,679,328,446 T3 batches in 1411 groups: the exact counts that P's charge multiplies by counted prices (proof 2.1, 6).

experiments.scope: Audit of pre-registrations C and D (proof 4.2, 4.3), stratum 0 of 5. Trial 0 audits a positive space of C: CPOS[0] (C's 23 positive spaces in (k, attempt) order, stratum = position mod 5), q0 = SHA-256(trial 0 seed) mod n. Trial 1 audits the success of a run completed by D: DPOS[0] (the first positive space of each of the 29 runs that D completed with an output, in k order, stratum = position mod 5; 6 entries), q1 = SHA-256(trial 1 seed) mod n. For the picked space (run k, attempt i, coordinate): B' re-derives run k's advice from its label ('hashsmash sha3-256-r5 v11 C B-prime run k': candidate setup c and accepting attempt j of CADV[k]); advice_ok iff the attempt is accepted, SHA-256 of the advice equals the log and the facts of proof 3 hold. Trial 0 re-runs the connector attempts 0..i of 'hashsmash sha3-256-r5 v11 C conn run k' and log_ok iff SHA-256 of their status string (accepted: chr(64 + DF), rejected: '-') equals the log, which fixes the space's place among the advice's accepted spaces; trial 1 re-runs attempt i only and log_ok iff it is accepted with the logged DF and work count (its place among the accepted spaces is in the per-run table of proof 4.3, not organizer-checked). Then the Python E (e_window) runs on the 2^12 aligned coordinates containing the logged one. A trial returns E's first output if both checks pass and the output is at the logged coordinate, otherwise no pair. Other trials return no pair. The seeds pick the audited spaces; in production the seed is the public seed, known in advance.
experiments.hypothesis: H1 numerator: successes of pre-registrations C and D are outputs of the specified algorithm (B', connector rule, E) run from their labels. Predicted: 2 full 5-round collisions of distinct 135-byte messages.
